📌 Tehran, IRNA — Commander-in-Chief of the Army Major General Amir Hatami says the Iranian Armed Forces will deliver a crushing response, should the enemy make another military mischief and threaten Iran.

General Hatami issued a warning to aggressors during his visit to Fars Province to inspect Army units stationed there, evaluating the personnel’s combat spirit, equipment readiness, and the units' defensive capabilities.
​
Commending the efforts, solidarity, and cooperation of the Armed Forces, the Commander-in-Chief of the Army also emphasized the need to maintain vigilance, stating that the war imposed by the US-Israeli enemy has not ended yet.
​
Referring to the recent wars and the armed forces’ achievements in affirming the Islamic Republic of Iran’s victory over its enemies, he said any conflict entails damage, but what matters is the outcome that brings honor and pride to the country.
​
General Hatami also stressed the need for any creative act capable of disrupting the enemy’s calculations, saying that the army personnel must seize the opportunities created to consolidate victory and keep the shadow of war away from the country, while maintaining steadfastness and resistance along their path.
​
Elsewhere, addressing a gathering of the families of martyrs, veterans, and Army combatants in Fars Province, the Army Commander-in-Chief paid tribute to their patience, patriotism, and allegiance to the Leader of the Islamic Revolution.

Parable: "Bread with Butter"

A man and his wife had been married for thirty years. On the morning of their anniversary, as she had done every year, the wife baked a small loaf of bread. At breakfast, she sliced it in half, spread butter on both pieces, and was about to hand her husband the soft crumb — just as she always had. But halfway through, she paused.

She thought: “Today, on our thirtieth anniversary, I want the crust for myself. I’ve dreamed of this for thirty years. I’ve been a devoted wife, raised wonderful sons, kept our home in perfect order — I deserve the crispy top.”

So she gave him the soft center instead — something she’d never allowed herself before. And as he took the bread, he smiled and said: “What a priceless gift you’ve given me today. Since childhood, I’ve loved the soft part of the bread. But because you always took it for yourself, I never dared ask.”

Moral: True love exists only where both are willing to give more than they take.

🔻 Russia hosts 8th round of regional talks on Afghanistan with Iran’s participation

📌 Moscow, IRNA – The eighth consultative meeting of the Moscow Format on Afghanistan has kicked off in the Russian capital, with delegations from 12 countries, including Iran, in attendance.

The meeting began on Monday, bringing together senior officials and special envoys from Iran, Russia, Afghanistan, India, Kazakhstan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, alongside representatives from Belarus and Egypt.
​
Director General for South Asian Affairs at Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mohammad Reza Bahrami, is heading a delegation at the Moscow Format that will begin its deliberations following the opening remarks by Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov.
​
Amir Khan Muttaqi, foreign minister of Afghanistan’s Taliban-led government and Pakistan’s special envoy in Kabul—whose countries have experienced cross-border military escalations in recent months—is present at the meeting.
​
Zamir Kabulov, the representative of the Russian president at the event, said earlier that special attention would be paid during Monday’s meeting to the Afghanistan-Pakistan conflict, announcing Moscow’s readiness to mediate between the two nations to achieve a lasting peace.
​
Meanwhile, Iran’s Ambassador to Russia Kazem Jalali, in a post on his X network, hailed the new round of the Moscow Format Consultative Meeting on Afghanistan, calling it a key step toward regional convergence.
​
He wrote that lasting peace and stability in Afghanistan will be achieved solely through the formation of an inclusive political structure involving all ethnic groups, reiterating opposition to any foreign military bases or infrastructure in the region.
​
The Moscow Format, established in 2017 at Russia’s initiative, is a regional mechanism for consultations regarding developments in Afghanistan and the country’s peace process.
